sections.title: JWST MEP - A World Under Spotty Starlight: Detection of CO2 and H2O in the Hot Saturn WASP-52b with JWST NIRSpec G395H
sections.abstract: JWST/NIRSpec transmission spectroscopy detects CO2 and confirms H2O in WASP-52b while modeling contamination from stellar spots and inhomogeneous clouds.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report the first CO2 detection for WASP-52b, confirmation of H2O, and evidence that starspots and high-altitude patchy clouds shape the spectrum.
sections.caveat: Composition, clouds, and stellar spots are degenerate; molecular abundances have order-of-magnitude uncertainties.

sections.title: LUX-ZEPLIN's Stairway to Heaνen: limits on elastic scatters of dark matter from solar capture
sections.abstract: The authors reinterpret the reported approximately 248 keV LUX-ZEPLIN recoil under elastic dark-matter operators and use solar capture plus neutrino observations to constrain those explanations.
sections.claimed_result: Solar capture and neutrino-flux data rule out broad weak-scale dark-matter mass ranges under the paper's elastic-scattering fits.
sections.caveat: Conclusions depend on reconstructed LZ Wilson coefficients and assumed annihilation final states.

sections.title: The AGN Channel in 3D: Scattering Belts and the Importance of Eccentricity in the Black Hole Population
sections.abstract: Three-dimensional hybrid N-body simulations of black holes in AGN disks show that direct binary encounters broaden merger formation around migration traps and that initial eccentricity can suppress mergers by roughly an order of magnitude.
sections.claimed_result: The authors find a scattering belt around the migration trap and estimate a gravitational-wave merger rate of approximately 2–12 Gpc^-3 yr^-1 under their modeled conditions.
sections.caveat: Rates and mass distributions are model-dependent and the simulation isolates dominant encounters rather than resolving every interaction.

sections.title: A computer assisted existence proof for a non-Schwarzschild black hole in Einstein--Weyl gravity
sections.abstract: A computer-assisted interval-arithmetic argument certifies the existence of a regular, asymptotically flat non-Schwarzschild black-hole solution in four-dimensional Einstein–Weyl gravity.
sections.claimed_result: The authors certify a regular nondegenerate horizon, no additional exterior horizon, zero Ricci scalar, and nonzero Ricci tensor.
sections.caveat: The proof establishes existence but not uniqueness, physical stability, or astrophysical formation.

sections.title: FLUMEN: Neural Emulator of an Advanced Stochastic Weak Lensing Model
sections.abstract: FLUMEN is a conditional normalizing-flow emulator for full weak-lensing magnification distributions across source redshift and cosmological parameters.
sections.claimed_result: The emulator reproduces Monte Carlo magnification distributions at negligible inference cost while enforcing relevant analytic distribution features.
sections.caveat: The emulator inherits assumptions and finite-resolution limitations of the underlying lensing model.
